sentences.text: Scientists estimated this creature measured between 6 and 8 meters in length and weighed approximately one ton.
Even when reaching its largest possible size, it remained smaller than other known members of its group.
The partial skeleton includes a largely intact pelvis, several vertebrae from the back and tail, and fragments of limb bones.
Unlike the related Baryonyx, this animal did not possess a bony horn core on its lacrimal bone.
Its lower jaw featured a large, oval opening on the side known as the mandibular fenestra.
The genus name reflects the frustration researchers felt because the skull had been heavily damaged by fossil collectors.
The specific name challengeri pays tribute to the fictional Professor Challenger from Arthur Conan Doyle's novels.
A recent study found bone structures in the skull consistent with salt glands, similar to those in seabirds.
The genus was first described by Martill and colleagues in 1996.
The holotype skull was found near Santana do Cariri in northeastern Brazil.
When discovered, the holotype skull was lying on its side.
Shortly after, in February 1996, Alexander W. A. Kellner and Diogenes de Almeida Campos described Angaturama limai from the same region.
A replica skeleton of Angaturama, built from postcranial material, became the first large carnivorous Brazilian dinosaur displayed to the public in March 2009.
Researchers suggest the animal likely preyed mainly on fish and other small animals it could catch.
Fossil evidence indicates an individual ate a pterosaur, either by hunting or scavenging.
Its elongated snout and unserrated conical teeth led scientists to theorize a partly fish-eating diet.
Smooth and homogeneous dental microwear suggests it consumed soft food.
A broad lower jaw and narrowed frontals caused its eye sockets to face steeply inward.
These skull traits allowed the animal to see above the waterline while submerged.
It possessed an enlarged flocculus, a brain structure associated with coordinating fast head movements.
Analysis of the cochlear duct suggests it could hear frequencies averaging 1,950 Hz with a bandwidth of 3,196 Hz.
The overall hearing range was estimated between 350 and 3,550 Hz, placing its ability between that of crocodiles and birds.
The tooth arrangement indicates continuous replacement where new teeth were pushed upward by old ones.
It shares dental features with Spinosaurus, including straight conical tooth crowns, thin enamel, unserrated edges, and lengthwise fluting.
Kellner later resolved the taxon as a spinosaurid and synonymized the family Irritatoridae with Spinosauridae.
The creature lived approximately 110 million years ago during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous Period.
It inhabited what is now South America during this same time.
The specimen most probably originates from the Romualdo Formation.
Researchers suggest the scarcity of herbivorous dinosaurs in the area may indicate that local vegetation was too sparse to support large populations.
Multiple authors from 2002 to 2015 supported the conclusion that Angaturama is a junior synonym of Irritator.
A 2018 publication argued that osteosclerosis would not have significantly changed a theropod's buoyancy.

In 2018, researchers argued that the holotype was buried in its natural habitat because the lower jaw remained attached to the skull, which would likely have detached if the carcass had floated at sea.
